title: Monpa and Apatani: Tawang to Ziro
price_note: Per person, twin sharing: best available stays including Rungkhung, Vivanta Tawang and Siiro Resort, all meals, private SUV with driver, private guide throughout, all sightseeing and e-ILP; flights extra.
transport: Private SUV with driver and private guide
meta_description: Signature Arunachal trip, 10 nights: Dirang, Tawang and Sela, then the Apatani valley of Ziro with a private guide, from ₹2,10,000 per person.
summary: Ten nights across two worlds of Arunachal: the Buddhist Monpa country of Dirang and Tawang, with its monasteries and high passes, and the Apatani rice valley of Ziro, with its clans, fields and festivals. Best available hotels, a private guide and a private SUV throughout.
intro: Most trips to Arunachal see either Tawang or Ziro. This one does both, and the contrast is the point. In the west you stay among Monpa monasteries, prayer flags and stone villages, at about 1,600–2,700 m. Then you cross back to the plains and climb again into the Apatani valley, where rice and fish grow in the same fields and villages are built of wood and bamboo.

We use the best stays in each place: Rungkhung Village Resort in Dirang, Vivanta Tawang, and Siiro Resort in Ziro. The night at Bhalukpong, which splits the long transfer, is the simplest of the trip, in the best available lodge by the Kameng. A private guide travels with you throughout, and in Ziro a guide from the Apatani community joins for village days.
highlights: Tawang Monastery and the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama
The crossing of Sela at about 4,170 m
Apatani villages of Hong and Hari with a local guide
Rice-and-fish terraces and pine groves of the Ziro valley

days.title: Tezpur to Dirang
days.text: Your guide and driver meet you in Tezpur, or in Guwahati with an earlier start. Drive through Balipara's tea gardens to the Bhalukpong check gate, then climb through Tenga and Bomdila and descend into the Dirang valley. Check into Rungkhung Village Resort among the orchards. Lunch is on the way at Bomdila. Arrive by late afternoon, in time for a short walk among the orchards before dinner. If you start from Guwahati, the drive is 3–4 hours longer and we leave very early or add a night on the plains.

days.title: Dirang Dzong and Sangti
days.text: An easy acclimatisation day at about 1,600 m. Walk through Dirang Dzong, the stone village with its fortified houses, and visit the hot springs. In the afternoon, drive to the Sangti valley for a riverside walk. Your guide introduces the Monpa: their Buddhist practice, their farming and their links with Bhutan and Tibet. Rest in the afternoon; tomorrow is the high crossing.

days.title: Over Sela to Tawang
days.text: Climb to Sela Pass, about 4,170 m, taking the old road for the lake when it is open. Stop at the Jaswantgarh memorial and at Nuranang Falls near Jang, then continue to Vivanta Tawang. Rest on arrival and drink plenty of water. Your guide watches for any sign of altitude discomfort and keeps the stop at the pass to 30–45 minutes. Avoid alcohol tonight and have an early dinner.

days.title: Tawang Monastery and Urgelling
days.text: Morning prayers at Tawang Monastery, then the museum and library with your guide. After lunch, visit Urgelling, birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama in 1683, and watch Mon shugu paper being made by hand. Sunset at the Tawang War Memorial. Your guide explains the murals, the giant Buddha image and the monastic routine. Dress modestly, walk clockwise around shrines and ask before photographing monks.

days.title: The high lakes
days.text: A full day above 4,000 m to Pangang Teng Tso and, where the road and Army rules allow, Sangetsar. Your guide carries hot drinks and lunch. Bum La can be added with extra permission. Back to the hotel by late afternoon. The road climbs through yak pastures, often under snow from December to April. If weather or Army rules close the road, your guide will plan a shorter outing instead.

days.title: Back to Dirang
days.text: A slow morning in Tawang, perhaps a visit to Ani Gompa or the carpet workshops, then drive back over Sela or through the tunnel to Rungkhung Village Resort for one more night in the orchards. Your driver times the crossing for the clearest part of the day. Dinner is at the resort, and the afternoon is free for a walk in the orchards or simply rest after the cold of Tawang.

days.title: Down to the Kameng at Bhalukpong
days.text: Drive down through Bomdila and Tenga to the plains at Bhalukpong. In the afternoon, walk the stony bank of the Kameng. Tonight's lodge is the simplest stay of the trip; it splits what would otherwise be a 12-hour transfer to Ziro. Lunch is at Bomdila or Tenga. The change from the cold of the hills to the warm, humid plains is sudden, so keep light clothes in your day bag. Keep permits handy for the exit check at the gate.

days.title: Across the plains and up to Ziro
days.text: A long day. Drive east along the north bank of the Brahmaputra through Gohpur, enter Arunachal again near Itanagar, and climb through Yazali to the Ziro valley. Your driver plans tea and lunch stops. Check into Siiro Resort, above the paddies, by early evening. Your guide carries your Inner Line Permit for Papum Pare and Lower Subansiri, checked on entry near Itanagar. Expect the last stretch from Yazali to be slow and winding.

days.title: Hong and Hari with an Apatani guide
days.text: A guide from the Apatani community joins you for Hong, one of the largest Apatani villages, and Hari. Walk among stilt houses, granaries and clan platforms, and learn how clans share land, forest and water. Ask before photographing anyone. Lunch is a home-cooked Apatani meal in a family house, by arrangement. The afternoon is free to rest or walk in the fields near the resort.

days.title: Fields, pine groves and pike pila
days.text: Walk the bunds of the rice-and-fish terraces with your guide, then climb into the pine and bamboo groves the clans manage on the hills. In the evening, join an Apatani kitchen session to make pike pila and smoked meat, and hear about tapyo, the old salt made from plant ash. Your guide can also take you to Hapoli market, where you may find Apatani textiles and smoked meats.

days.title: Ziro to Donyi Polo Airport
days.text: Drive down from the valley through Yazali to Donyi Polo Airport at Hollongi, near Itanagar, for an afternoon flight. If your flight is late, there is time for a stop in Itanagar on the way. Check flight timings carefully, since departures from Donyi Polo Airport are limited and schedules change. In the monsoon months we leave extra time for landslides on the Ziro road. Say goodbye to your guide and driver at the terminal.

good_to_know: Sela is about 4,170 m and the lakes above 4,000 m; two nights in Dirang first help with acclimatisation. Talk to your doctor if you have heart or lung conditions.
Day 8 is a long transfer of 9–10 hours; the Bhalukpong night is simple but splits the journey.
Ziro has no luxury hotel; Siiro Resort is the most comfortable stay in the valley.
Your e-ILP must list West Kameng, Tawang, Papum Pare and Lower Subansiri. Check current status before you travel.
For the Ziro Festival of Music in late September, book everything by early summer.

faqs.q: Why combine Tawang and Ziro in one trip?
faqs.a: They show two very different sides of Arunachal: Buddhist Monpa highlands in the west and the Apatani farming valley in the centre. Together they give a far fuller picture than either alone.

Ten nights in the best available stays with all meals, a private SUV and driver, a private guide throughout plus an Apatani guide in Ziro, and all fees, for two sharing. Flights, drinks and tips are extra. Indicative 2026 price.

faqs.q: Why is there a night at Bhalukpong?
faqs.a: Tawang to Ziro is too far for one or even two comfortable days. A night at Dirang and one at Bhalukpong on the plains edge split it. The Bhalukpong lodge is simple, but the next day is shorter and safer.

faqs.q: Is Ziro comfortable enough for a signature trip?
faqs.a: Ziro has no luxury hotel. Siiro Resort has comfortable wooden rooms with attached bathrooms and is the best stay in the valley. What makes Ziro special is time with Apatani families, which a guide arranges.

faqs.q: When is the best time for this trip?
faqs.a: March to April and October to November, when both Tawang and Ziro are at their best. Late September brings the Ziro Festival of Music but some rain. Winter is possible but cold in Tawang.
Only on the Tawang section, where Sela and the lakes are above 4,000 m. Two nights in Dirang first help most people. Ziro is at about 1,500–1,700 m.

faqs.q: Can we fly out of Ziro?
faqs.a: Ziro's small airport has had limited regional flights. Donyi Polo Airport near Itanagar is more reliable, about 4–5 hours by road. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is this trip suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes, for seniors in good health who can manage several long drives. The pace includes rest days, and the guide can adapt walks. Talk to your doctor about the altitude on the Tawang days.

Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit listing West Kameng, Tawang, Papum Pare and Lower Subansiri; we arrange it. Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit through a registered operator. Check current status before you travel.
